question: What percentage of voters will support Edgewater, Florida's 2026 referendum to ban data centers?

calls.reasoning: The only voter-enacted city data-center ban found (Monterey Park, CA, June 2026) passed with 88%, but that was a contested fight over a real proposed project. Edgewater's measure was referred unanimously by its own council, has no organized opposition found, and national polls show broad bipartisan skepticism of data centers. Pulling the number down: Volusia County leans conservative, several charter amendments share the ballot, and voters may see the measure as redundant with the ordinance already in force. Edgewater's 2024 business-tax-exemption referendum split ~50/50, so city measures there do not pass automatically. No human prediction market was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Median ~75%.
sources: Volusia County 2024 general election results (Edgewater business tax exemption referendum) via web search
calls.dossier:
- Measure: Edgewater (Volusia County, FL) Charter Amendment 4, Nov 3 2026 ballot; would amend the city charter to prohibit permitting/construction/expansion/operation of new data centers (hyperscale, AI, crypto mining). (Ballotpedia; MultiState 2026-09-24)
- The council voted unanimously to put it on the ballot (Aug 2026, ClickOrlando 2026-08-04) and unanimously passed a permanent ban ordinance (Sept 14 2026, Fox35) as a bridge to the charter amendment. Rationale given: a future council could repeal the ordinance, while a charter amendment can only be changed by voters.
- No data center has been proposed in Edgewater; the ban is preemptive (wendyrealtor blog, Fox35).
- Resident public comment at council meetings opposed data centers on noise, job claims and NDA/transparency grounds; no organized opposition campaign found.
- Comparable: Monterey Park, CA Measure NDC (June 2026) passed 10,321-1,362 = 88.3%. That was contested and followed a real proposed project. (LA Public Press, June 2026)
- National polling: 2026 Reuters/Ipsos found 64% don't think rapidly building data centers is good, 77% worry about electricity rates, and 14% would live near one.
- Local electorate: Edgewater's Nov 2024 business-tax-exemption referendum failed 49.8% yes vs 50.2% no (6,684 vs 6,733 votes, about 13.4k total). The same election's DeBary term-limits amendment passed at 64%. Volusia leans Republican.
- Other 2026 data-center measures (KS, IL, OH) have not been voted on yet; no results available.
- Status quo: the ordinance ban is already in force either way; the amendment adds charter-level durability.
- Resolves off official results for Edgewater 'yes' share, rounded; this is not a pass/fail question.
- Event window: election Nov 3 2026; as of Oct 22 2026, early/mail voting is underway and results are not yet in.
- Searched, absent: any poll of the measure, the exact ballot wording (the Ballotpedia fetch came back empty), how many other charter amendments share the ballot, any human prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Local US data-center ban/moratorium ballot measures and uncontested council-referred municipal charter amendments in small Florida cities

calls.reasoning: Reference class: uncontested council-referred local restriction/charter amendments plus the only voter-enacted data center ban precedent (Monterey Park CA, June 2026, ~86-88% yes amid an active fight over a real project). Edgewater measure is unanimously council-backed with no organized opposition found, a county-wide ban just passed 6-0 and an ordinance already in place; polling shows 56-78% support for bans/moratoria generally, lower among Republicans (Edgewater leans R, older). No proposed project means lower salience, and some charter-amendment reflexive 'no'. No market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers. Median ~73%.
calls.dossier:
- Edgewater FL (Volusia County, ~25k pop) Charter Amendment 4 on Nov 3, 2026 ballot: would bar permitting, construction, expansion or operation of new data centers in city limits (ClickOrlando 2026-08-04; Multistate 2026-09-24).
- City council voted unanimously to place it on the ballot and also made a related moratorium permanent by ordinance (ClickOrlando Aug 2026; Fox35). Mayor Diezel DePew backs it, citing water/aquifer and power concerns (MyNews13 2026-07-21).
- No specific data center project is proposed in Edgewater; the ban is preemptive (ClickOrlando; wendyrealtor blog).
- No organized opposition found in news coverage; local environmental group Dream Green Volusia supports it.
- Volusia County Council voted 6-0 to ban large-scale data centers in unincorporated areas (MyNews13 2026-10-21); Ormond Beach has a moratorium.
- Precedent: Monterey Park CA Measure NDC (June 2, 2026): about 86-88% yes (10,321 to 1,362), the first voter-enacted citywide ban, after an active fight over a proposed 247k sq ft project; Democratic-leaning LA County city (LA Public Press; Climate Change News 2026-06-17).
- Polls: NJ 56% support local bans (Stockton, May 2026); WI 67% support a 1-year construction ban, 83% of Democrats vs 53% of Republicans (Marquette, Aug 2026); Ohio 78% support a temporary ban (BGSU, Sep 2026).
- Edgewater/Volusia lean Republican, with an older electorate.
- Status quo: an ordinance ban is already in effect; the amendment would entrench it in the charter.
- Resolves off official yes percentage for the measure (Ballotpedia/official results), rounded.
- Event window: Nov 3, 2026 election; as of Oct 22 the vote has not happened (early/mail voting under way).
- Searched but not found: ballot wording text, any Edgewater-specific poll, any opposition campaign spending, any market.
calls.reference_class: Local data-center ban ballot measures and uncontested council-referred municipal charter amendments restricting land use

calls.reasoning: Reference class: local data-center ban measures and uncontested Florida municipal charter amendments. Monterey Park, CA passed its ban in June 2026 with 88.3%. Small-city Florida charter amendments without organized opposition typically pass with 60-80%. Edgewater's council voted unanimously, already enacted the same ban by ordinance on Sept 14, 2026, and no data center is proposed there. I found no organized 'No' campaign. Data-center opposition is bipartisan, which matters in a Republican-leaning Volusia County city. Two things push the share down: Florida voters' general habit of voting no on charter changes and down-ballot confusion, and some voters may see the measure as redundant or anti-business. No human market was found: the harness found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold, and I found nothing on Kalshi or with bookmakers. My median is 76.
calls.dossier:
- Measure: Edgewater (Volusia County, FL) Charter Amendment 4 asks whether to prohibit the permitting, construction, expansion or operation of new data centers (hyperscale, AI, crypto mining) in city limits. Vote is Nov 3, 2026 (Ballotpedia; MultiState, 2026-09-24).
- The council voted unanimously in early Aug 2026 to put it on the ballot. On Sept 14, 2026 the council enacted a permanent ban by ordinance, effective immediately. The charter amendment would make the ban durable against future councils (ClickOrlando 2026-08-04; Fox35).
- No data center has been proposed in Edgewater; the ban is preemptive (Fox35, wendyrealtor blog).
- At council meetings, public comment opposed data centers, citing noise, few lasting jobs, and NDAs (ClickOrlando).

- About 28-35 localities have data-center measures on the Nov 2026 ballot; no results are out yet (MultiState; Newsweek).
- Base rates: uncontested Florida small-city charter amendments typically get about 55-80% yes. That rate is general, not specific to data centers, and I counted it from general knowledge, not a dataset. Over voter-enacted data-center bans so far there is one case, at 88%.
- Edgewater is a Republican-leaning city of about 25k. Polls show data-center opposition is bipartisan.
- Searched and found nothing: Edgewater-specific polls, campaign finance filings for a No side, the exact ballot wording.
- Resolution: resolves off official yes-% results (Volusia County Supervisor of Elections / Ballotpedia), rounded.

calls.reference_class: Local data-center ban ballot measures (2026) and uncontested Florida municipal charter amendments

calls.reasoning: Anchor: uncontested council-referred FL municipal charter amendments typically get ~60-80% yes; the only voter-enacted data-center ban (Monterey Park CA, Jun 2026) got 88% in a contested fight over a real project. Edgewater's measure has unanimous council backing, no organized opposition, a fresh 6-0 Volusia County ban raising salience, and polls show bipartisan anti-data-center sentiment. Downward pulls: no proposed project (low salience), redundancy with the existing ordinance, a reflexive 'no' on charter changes among some voters, and Edgewater's 2024 tax referendum split ~50/50. Median 75.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agree on all facts: Monterey Park at 88.3%, the council's unanimous referral, the Sept 14 ordinance already in force, no organized opposition, no proposed project, no market found. Their medians (73/75/76) differ only in how they weigh the low salience and Republican lean against broad anti-data-center sentiment and the Volusia County ban. No evidence breaks that tie; I take 75 with a width of about 24, consistent with all three runs.

disagreements.claim: How much the Republican/older electorate lowers support
disagreements.verdict: Modest effect; anti-data-center sentiment is bipartisan and older Florida voters lean protective. Not settled by evidence.

disagreements.claim: Whether redundancy with the existing ordinance and the absence of a project depress the yes share
disagreements.verdict: Some depressive effect relative to Monterey Park's 88%; this is reflected in the median of 75.

disagreements.claim: Weight of the 2024 Edgewater tax referendum (49.8% yes) as a local signal
disagreements.verdict: Weak relevance: that was a tax giveaway to businesses, a different valence; it informs the lower tail only.
